title: Ballad of the Sun Maiden and the Moon Brother (Ka Rwai Ka Sngi bad U Bnai)
khasi_title: Ka Rwai Ka Sngi bad U Bnai
cultural_context: In Khasi cosmology, the Sun (Ka Sngi) is female—the glorious maternal source of life and truth—while the Moon (U Bnai) is her younger brother. According to the ancient myth celebrated in song, the young brother developed improper desires toward his sister. In righteous indignation, Ka Sngi cast a handful of hot fireplace ashes (Dpei) directly across his face, permanently blemishing his visage with dark grey spots. Shamed, U Bnai retreated to traverse only the cool, solitary darkness of the night, while Ka Sngi reigns over radiant daylight.
lyrics_khasi:
Ko Ka Sngi ba phyrnai, ko Mei ka jingshai,
Mei-rad jong ka bneng, ka pyrthei Me pynim;
Ha suin Me phriang ki kjat sngi ba kordor,
Ban bsa ia ki sim, ki syntiew, ki briew.

U Bnai uba rit, u hymmen ba bieit,
U kwah ban leh bakla ia la ka jong ka hynmen;
Ka Sngi ka la bitar, ka shim ia ka dpei,
Kha-khi ka theh halor ka khmat jong u bnai!

Kumta u Bnai u kylla pait-lieh pait-iong,
U lehrain ban mih ha ka sngi ba shai kdar;
U iaid tang mynmiet ha ka dum ka syngken,
Da ka khmat ba thoh-dpei ba sniew ka dur.

Ko Mei Ka Sngi, to iai ai ka jingshai,
Ban pynneh ia ka Hok, ban kyntait ia ka Sang;
Ha pyrthei to iai sawa ka nam jong Ka Sngi,
Ka kmie ka kynrad ba bsa ia ka Ri!
lyrics_english:
O radiant Sun Maiden, Mother of eternal light,
Great mother of the heavens, giving life to all the earth;
Across the blue vault Thou spreadest Thy golden beams,
Nourishing the birds, the flowers, and mortal beings.

Young Moon, foolish and undisciplined brother,
Conceived forbidden desire toward his own elder sister;
The Sun blazed in wrath, seized hearthside ashes,
And hurled them blazing across the face of the Moon!

Hence the Moon became stained with dark blemish,
Ashamed forever to appear in broad golden daylight;
He wanders alone in the chill silence of the night,
Bearing forever the ash-stained mark of shame.

O Mother Sun, continually grant us Thy celestial light,
To preserve our righteousness and cast out moral transgression;
Throughout the earth let the renown of the Sun Maiden resound,
The queen and mother who sustains the sacred land!

stanzas.title: Ka Sngi Ka Kmie Jong Ka Jingshai (The Sun Mother of Light)
stanzas.khasi:
Ko Ka Sngi ba phyrnai, ko Mei ka jingshai,
Mei-rad jong ka bneng, ka pyrthei Me pynim;
Ha suin Me phriang ki kjat sngi ba kordor,
Ban bsa ia ki sim, ki syntiew, ki briew.
stanzas.english: O radiant Sun Maiden, mother of heavens and light, nourishing blossoms, beasts, and mankind with Thy golden rays.

stanzas.title: Ka Dpei Halor U Bnai (Ashes upon the Moon's Face)
stanzas.khasi:
U Bnai uba rit, u hymmen ba bieit,
U kwah ban leh bakla ia la ka jong ka hynmen;
Ka Sngi ka la bitar, ka shim ia ka dpei,
Kha-khi ka theh halor ka khmat jong u bnai!
stanzas.english: When the foolish brother overstepped clan boundaries, the Sun Maiden in holy wrath cast fireplace ashes across his face.

stanzas.title: Ka Jingiaid Mynmiet (The Nightly Solitary Wanderer)
stanzas.khasi:
Kumta u Bnai u kylla pait-lieh pait-iong,
U lehrain ban mih ha ka sngi ba shai kdar;
U iaid tang mynmiet ha ka dum ka syngken,
Da ka khmat ba thoh-dpei ba sniew ka dur.
stanzas.english: Ash-spotted and ashamed to behold the day, the Moon traverses alone through the cold nocturnal shadows.

stanzas.title: Ka Jingiaroh ia Ka Sngi (Praise to the Sun Mother)
stanzas.khasi:
Ko Mei Ka Sngi, to iai ai ka jingshai,
Ban pynneh ia ka Hok, ban kyntait ia ka Sang;
Ha pyrthei to iai sawa ka nam jong Ka Sngi,
Ka kmie ka kynrad ba bsa ia ka Ri!
stanzas.english: O Mother Sun, preserve truth and banish incestuous taboo; let Thy glory shine forever across the motherland!

vocabulary.ka sngi: The sun; female deity and maternal life-giver in Khasi theology
vocabulary.u bnai: The moon; male celestial entity, brother to the sun
vocabulary.ka sang: Moral taboo, incest, or cardinal spiritual violation in Khasi law
vocabulary.thoh-dpei: Spotted or stained with gray ashes
